### Samson Avenges Himself on the Philistines
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/samson-avenges-himself
Passage: Judges 15:16
Points:
- Samson was driven by carnality and personal vengeance rather than God's honor.
- The men of Judah revealed spiritual apathy by arresting Samson to appease their oppressors.
- God sovereignly accomplished His purposes against Philistine oppression despite Samson's flawed motives.
- Samson was brought to recognize his weakness and pray only when overcome by severe thirst.
- Believers should be humbled that God mercifully redeems and uses deeply flawed servants.

### When God’s Victory Hides Under the Mess
Author: Davy Ellison
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/victory-under-mess/
Passage: Judges 15:1-20
Points:
- Samson pursued a destructive personal vendetta that ignored God's glory.
- The men of Judah chose compromise over faith by betraying their own deliverer.
- Judah’s betrayal of Samson foreshadows the handing over of Jesus to maintain peace with Rome.
- The Spirit of the Lord granted miraculous victory even while Samson took credit for himself.
- God works through broken people and messy situations to accomplish His redemptive plans.

### My Thirsty Heart
Author: Luann Prater
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement-cafe/my-thirsty-heart-encouragement-caf-december-31-2018.html
Passage: Judges 15:18
Points:
- Hectic schedules and constant demands leave the human soul parched and exhausted.
- Relying on personal strength during difficult moments leads to spiritual burnout.
- Difficult seasons reveal our helplessness and force a choice between self-reliance and God.
- Like Samson crying out after his battle, believers must acknowledge their emptiness to the Lord.
- God responds with life-giving refreshment when His weary children call upon Him.

### Weakness in Triumph
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-january-21-2016.html
Passage: Judges 15:18
Points:
- Believers frequently find small daily troubles overwhelming right after experiencing major spiritual triumphs.
- God uses sudden physical or emotional limits to keep His people humble and dependent.
- Samson’s boastful celebration was swiftly halted by thirst, compelling him to cry out in prayer.
- Experiencing profound weakness during moments of success is a normal part of the Christian walk.
- The same Lord who granted past deliverance provides sustaining water for present needs.
